sermon.title: The Third Reason Sheep Go Astray
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the third reason sheep go astray: their shepherds cause them to stray. He names hireling leaders, wrong doctrines and distractions in the church, tells stories from his Detroit childhood of children harmed while authorities did nothing, and calls the church to unite. God’s solution is pastors after his heart who feed with knowledge, with authority restored.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: Ezekiel 34 read as unfulfilled global prophecy; “four awakenings”; prophecy called the initial evidence of the Holy Ghost; Jerusalem read as the church; Philippines claim of half a million drug dealers surrendering in seven weeks and Singapore claims (unverified). Sensitive content kept as spoken: Catholic idols, Mary and penance; Trump and Norman Vincent Peale; Rick Warren named; childhood stories of a friend shot, a boy’s suicide and a girl’s assault (private people named in transcript only); Obama and Hillary on negotiation; Philippine president executing drug dealers; homosexual activists; drunkards to hell.

chunks.section_question: What does he say would prevent these things?

faqs.answer: Church leaders—hirelings who care about what they get from the sheep.

faqs.answer: He says the apostles are the twelve.

faqs.answer: God delivering his sheep from bad shepherds globally.

faqs.answer: Prophecy—speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

faqs.question: Do all speak in tongues?
faqs.answer: No—the Bible plainly says they don’t.

faqs.question: Do dress rules make people holy?
faqs.answer: He says they replace the Ten Commandments with man-made rules.
